owner: CC builds it; cairn/tools/artifact is a TOOL (users, not owners — Law 6): the journal it appends is the record repo's state, owned by whoever owns that repo's records, and the door gates nothing at its own address

watchme.trigger: every append to either .artifact-journal.jsonl — the door pokes the probe after the write, so the probe costs nothing between writes and no poller exists (memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll).
watchme.enough: 500 journaled writes spanning all three caller classes with ZERO caller=unknown entries, AND the hand-edit escape route exercised at least once end to end (a ruling opened by the door and confirmed or refused by Akien). ONE unknown is the finding, not noise: it means a writer exists whose ancestry the door cannot read, which is the WRONG-INTENT clause of the falsifier. The watch does not clear on a timer.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, naming the caller-class histogram, every unknown entry with its raw cgroup path, and the hand-edit rulings opened.
watchme.nexus: the who-writes-what tree — the same journal the counting learning block (third ticket of the ruling) reads; this probe is that block's first consumer and defines the frequency table it will predict from.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and the counting learning block once cast.

children: none, because the two follow-ons named in the intent berth (rename the record classes to .artifact through the door; a counting learning block over the journal) DEPEND on this door existing rather than decompose it — a child proves before its parent, and neither can prove before the door does. They are cast as their own tickets with depends_on this id when this ticket reaches PROVEME, under the same ruling (CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-13-records-of-truth-change-only-through-the-artifact-door.json).
